newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS Holding sees more Swiss share buybacks.
newsitem.headline: CS Holding sees more Swiss share buybacks.

text.p: CS Holding said it expected Swiss share buybacks to become increasingly popular and said schemes to cut stocks' par value alone could chop market capitalisation by nearly one percent over the next two years.
"We expect the number of capital repayments to rise significantly in Switzerland," it said in a research note.

"This will lead to an improved supply/demand ratio on the bourse. The extra money paid out should for the most part flow back into the share market," it added, suggesting firms clearly focused on core businesses would profit most from this trend.
Tax considerations make capital repayments stemming from reductions in stocks' par value the most elegant way to conduct share buybacks, CS Research said.

It expected such schemes to pay back shareholders four billion to five billion Swiss francs over the next two years, or nearly one percent of current market capitalisation. The big three banks could do the biggest such operations.

Direct share buybacks are more difficult for tax reasons, but could increasingly emerge because several companies have exhausted their potential to cut shares' par values to the legal minimum of 10 francs.

It said high capital ratios at Novartis AG -- to be formed by the merger of Sandoz AG and Ciba-Geigy AG -- and Roche Holding AG made them theoretical candidates for share buybacks, but that they would probably use the funds for the time being to invest in future growth.
